question: Which embryonic germ layer develops into all the connective tissues in the body?
explanation: Mesenchyme is the specific embryonic tissue layer that gives rise to the various types of connective tissues found in the human body. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T7#BMP111_U1_T7_h1)

question: How do connective tissues structurally differ from epithelial tissues?

options.A: Connective tissues have cells scattered within a non-living matrix rather than tightly packed sheets
options.B: Connective tissues lack a blood supply entirely while epithelial tissues are heavily vascularized
options.C: Connective tissues consist exclusively of living cells with no extracellular material between them
options.D: Connective tissues cover internal and external body surfaces while epithelial tissues anchor organs

explanation: Epithelial tissue forms close-knit cellular sheets, whereas connective tissue consists of cells separated by an extracellular matrix. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T7#BMP111_U1_T7_h1)

question: Which main cell type produces the protein fibers and ground substance of connective tissue?
explanation: Fibroblasts are the most common cells in connective tissues, and they constantly secrete collagen, elastic fibers, and ground substance. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T7#BMP111_U1_T7_h2)

question: What is the primary function of elastic fibers in connective tissue?

options.A: Allowing tissues to stretch and return to their original shape
options.B: Anchoring epithelial cells tightly to the underlying basement membrane
options.C: Forming a rigid supportive framework inside solid organs
options.D: Providing maximum resistance against heavy compressive loads

explanation: Elastic fibers contain the protein elastin, which gives structures like blood vessels and lung tissue the ability to recoil after stretching. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T7#BMP111_U1_T7_h2)

question: Which type of connective tissue forms tendons and ligaments because of its parallel collagen bundles?
explanation: Dense regular tissue features fibers running in the same direction, giving it great strength when pulled along that single axis. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T7#BMP111_U1_T7_h3)

question: Why is dense irregular connective tissue well-suited for the deep layer of the skin (dermis)?

options.A: It provides a soft spongy bed for easy diffusion of oxygen and nutrients
options.B: It resists pulling forces coming from many different directions at once
options.C: It contracts actively to generate body heat when environmental temperatures drop
options.D: It stores large amounts of triglycerides to insulate the body against cold

explanation: Because its collagen fibers are bundled in various orientations, dense irregular tissue withstands mechanical stress from multiple directions. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T7#BMP111_U1_T7_h3)

question: What are the mature cells found inside small spaces (lacunae) of cartilage called?
explanation: Chondrocytes are the primary living cells of mature cartilage, residing in small spaces called lacunae within the firm matrix. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T7#BMP111_U1_T7_h4)

question: How does the lack of a direct blood supply affect cartilage tissue?

options.A: It relies entirely on active transport proteins on the cell surface to pump in oxygen
options.B: It becomes extremely hard and brittle due to the rapid deposition of calcium phosphate
options.C: It heals very slowly after an injury because nutrients must diffuse from nearby tissues
options.D: It undergoes constant remodeling and daily turnover driven by osteoclast activity

explanation: Cartilage lacks direct blood vessels, which makes metabolic exchange slow and means tissue repair takes a long time. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T7#BMP111_U1_T7_h4)

question: What is the liquid extracellular matrix of blood called?
explanation: Plasma is the fluid portion of blood that suspends red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T7#BMP111_U1_T7_h5)

question: Why are blood and lymph classified as connective tissues despite being liquids?

options.A: They connect the external environment directly to the internal organs of the body
options.B: They develop from embryonic mesenchyme and consist of cells embedded in an extracellular matrix
options.C: They contain large amounts of fibrous collagen proteins that circulate freely in the vessels
options.D: They provide mechanical shock absorption for the skeletal joints during physical movement

explanation: Despite being liquid, blood and lymph share the same embryonic origin and cellular-matrix makeup as other connective tissues. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T7#BMP111_U1_T7_h5)

question: A pregnant woman presents with poor wound healing and fragile gums due to a dietary deficiency. Which vitamin necessary for collagen synthesis is likely lacking?
explanation: Vitamin C is essential for forming collagen; a deficiency impairs structural repair in connective tissues like gums and skin. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T7#BMP111_U1_T7_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical feature of disorders affecting structural connective tissue proteins like collagen?

options.A: Uncontrolled rapid contraction of skeletal muscle fibers
options.B: Skeletal weakness or pathological bone fractures
options.D: Abnormal skin fragility and easy bruising

explanation: Muscle contraction is the function of muscle tissue proteins like actin and myosin, not the extracellular matrix proteins of connective tissues. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T7#BMP111_U1_T7_h6)
